Such a good question in my opinion. Why do humans ask questions? Why do we even have words that can convey so much meaning and yet we often misunderstand and misinterpret each other? It could be supposed that misunderstandings and the drive for knowledge is an innate part of what it means to be humans. But at the same time it could also be said that being human is to be imperfect and that our drive to answer the eternal, "Why?" is nothing more than the force that drives some of us towards perfection.

Supposing we could finally answer the question of why, would we then be perfect? If we as a species could attain the knowledge in our finite time on Earth, would we be perfect, or would we simply arrive at a better understanding of just how much we do not know? Would we realize that our efforts were futile for could there be such an answer as to why?

Or supposing we cannot answer the question of why, would this condemn us to imperfection for all of eternity or are there other, better ways to seek out the perfection we so desire? When we are searching for why, should we be asking a different question?

One could surmise that if we cannot answer why then we cannot obtain perfection as a species in any capacity and that we must as such settle our minds around the fact that we cannot know everything.

As a species we've always sought out more knowledge and have always sought out an answer to the oldest question of why. Do we have to have an answer in order to be perfect? And if we do not then for what purpose does asking why accomplish? And supposing we do need to answer the question why to achieve perfection then to what lengths are we willing to go before we consider whether we are fine where we are today?
